steps: Identify the useful energy output and total energy input (or use power values)
Calculate efficiency = useful energy output ÷ total energy input
Multiply by 100 to express as a percentage
Find wasted energy = total input − useful output
method_card.title: Efficiency and Energy Resources
method_card.content:
Efficiency is a ratio — it has no unit. It tells you what fraction of the input energy is transferred usefully.

Key equations:

  • Efficiency = useful energy transferred ÷ total energy transferred
  • Efficiency = useful power output ÷ total power input (works because time cancels)
  • Wasted energy = total input − useful output

Common pitfalls:

  • Putting wasted energy in the numerator instead of useful energy
  • Writing units (J or W) after an efficiency answer — it is dimensionless
  • Confusing efficiency as a decimal (e.g. 0.36) with efficiency as a percentage (36%)

exam_context.frequency: High — efficiency appears in most physics papers

gold.display: A coal power station generates 800 MW of electrical power from a thermal input of 2,000 MW. Calculate the efficiency as a percentage. Calculate how much power is wasted in MW.
A device has efficiency 0.65. In 30 seconds it uses 1,500 J of input energy. Calculate the useful energy output in 30 seconds.
A gas boiler has efficiency 0.85. It needs to deliver 12,750 J of useful heat energy. Calculate the total energy input required.
A student tests two lamps. Lamp A: 40 W input, 8 W light output. Lamp B: 12 W input, 3 W light output. Which is more efficient? Enter the efficiency of Lamp A as a decimal.

misconceptions.message: Lamp A: 8/40 = 0.20. Lamp B: 3/12 = 0.25. Lamp B is more efficient (0.25 > 0.20).

bronze.display: A device uses 200 J of energy and produces 50 J of useful output. Calculate its efficiency as a decimal.

misconceptions.message: Use useful output (50 J) in the numerator, not wasted energy. Efficiency = 50 ÷ 200 = 0.25.

bronze.display: A light bulb takes in 60 J and transfers 12 J as light. Calculate the efficiency as a percentage.

misconceptions.message: Multiply the ratio by 100 to get a percentage: (12/60) × 100 = 20%.

bronze.display: A device has a total energy input of 500 J. Its useful output is 350 J. How much energy is wasted?
A motor has useful power output of 300 W and total power input of 400 W. Calculate its efficiency as a decimal.
An electric kettle has efficiency 0.92. If the total input power is 2,000 W, calculate the useful power output.
A car engine takes in 60,000 J and has an efficiency of 0.30. Calculate the useful energy output.

silver.display: A wind turbine has a power input of 8,000 W from the wind and a useful electrical power output of 2,800 W. Calculate its efficiency as a percentage.
A device has efficiency 0.45 and useful power output of 900 W. Calculate the total power input.
A light bulb has efficiency 0.15. It has a power input of 60 W. Calculate the rate at which energy is wasted.
silver.equation_hint: Wasted = total input − useful output. Useful = efficiency × total.

silver.display: A car engine takes in 50,000 J and delivers 18,000 J of useful kinetic energy. Calculate the efficiency and the wasted energy. Enter the wasted energy in joules.

worked_examples.question: A light bulb takes in 60 J of electrical energy each second and transfers 12 J as light. Calculate its efficiency.
A motor has a total power input of 400 W. Its useful power output is 300 W. Calculate efficiency and the rate at which energy is wasted.
A car engine takes in 50,000 J of chemical energy from fuel. It delivers 18,000 J as useful kinetic energy. Calculate the efficiency and the wasted energy.
